metadata.description: TCImpact Socratic Question Bank for Agent 1 student coaching
metadata.philosophy: Never tell students what to do. Ask questions that help them discover how to improve their own project. Empowerment over instruction.
metadata.tci_alignment: Matches TCI's core empowerment philosophy from the learning labs
metadata.usage: Agent 1 selects questions using the question engine logic below
notes: Students may be from underserved, Indigenous, or climate-affected communities — questions must honor that context
Never deploy high-rigor questions when student is expressing discouragement
Never propose a solution before asking at least two reflective questions
Always close an interaction block with a growth reflection question

question_engine_logic.description: Agent 1 follows this sequence for every student interaction
steps: 1. Detect emotion signal (discouragement, anxiety, excitement, stuck)
2. Detect project signal (too small, missing evidence, blocker, math anxiety)
3. Select category based on signals (see signal_detection below)
4. Filter questions by depth_level appropriate to student
5. Check cooldown — exclude any subcategory used in last 3 exchanges
7. Add optional follow_up_prompt if student response is brief
8. Close interaction block with a growth_reflection question
9. Occasionally mirror a strength (see strength_language pool)
question_engine_logic.anti_directive_rule: Never propose a solution before asking at least two reflective questions
question_engine_logic.max_depth_escalation: Start at depth_level 1, escalate only after student demonstrates engagement

signal_detection.description: Keyword pattern matching to route to correct question category

math_confidence_scaling.description: Before scaffolding En-ROADS math, ask confidence level first
math_confidence_scaling.prompt: On a scale of 1 to 5, how confident do you feel about this calculation right now?

routing.1_2: Deploy gentle scaffold — MCB_1 through MCB_4 first

growth_reflection_questions.description: Always close an interaction block with one of these. Builds metacognition.
questions: What feels clearer now than it did at the start of this conversation?
What is one new idea you have that you did not have before?
What small next step feels possible right now?
What is the most useful thing you discovered today?
What would you tell another student who was just starting this project?

strength_language_pool.description: Agent 1 occasionally mirrors student strengths. Especially powerful for Indigenous and underserved students. Use sparingly — once per conversation maximum.
phrases: It sounds like you are thinking deeply about this.
You noticed something really important there.
The fact that you are asking this question shows real insight.
You are already thinking like an environmental scientist.
That kind of thinking is exactly what makes projects like this matter.
It takes courage to take on a challenge like this.

context_sensitivity_flags.description: Some questions assume community access. Route differently if student indicates rural isolation, small school, or limited internet.
context_sensitivity_flags.routing_note: If context_sensitive question would be irrelevant, skip to next question in same subcategory

question_bank.description: For projects that are too small, too safe, or missing community connections

questions.follow_up_prompt: What makes you say that?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Can you give an example?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What makes you say that?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What excites you most about that?
questions.question: If your project lasted for five years instead of five weeks, what might be different?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Can you tell me more about that?
questions.question: What part of this issue feels biggest or most urgent in your community?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would be the most important thing to pass on?
questions.question: If another school wanted to copy your idea, what would they need from you?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would the headline be?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would need to be true for that to happen?

questions.follow_up_prompt: How might you connect with them?
questions.question: Who in your community is already working on something related to this?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would it take to include them?
questions.question: Whose voices are most affected by this issue, and have they been included in your thinking?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What might they say that would surprise you?
questions.question: Are there elders, local leaders, or cultural knowledge keepers who might see this differently?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What causes that difference?
questions.question: How does this issue show up differently in different neighborhoods around you?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Can you give an example?
questions.question: Who might benefit the most if your project succeeds?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would you ask them for?
questions.question: Is there a local business, organization, or tribal council that might care about this topic?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Who in your community experiences that most directly?
questions.question: How might this issue connect to jobs, health, or daily life in your area?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Why do you think they might see it that way?
questions.question: If you asked someone younger than you about this issue, what might they say?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What did you find?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would a fair test of that look like?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Which of those feels most important to account for?
questions.question: What variables might influence the outcome of your project?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would you say if they pushed back?
questions.question: If someone challenged your idea, what evidence would you use to explain it?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What else does that system connect to?
questions.question: How does your project connect to larger systems like climate, energy, or food systems?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Why do you think that is?
questions.question: Who does this issue affect most, and why?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Can you give an example from your own community?
questions.question: How do history or culture shape this problem in your community?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Is that fair? Why or why not?
questions.question: Who pays the costs of this issue, and who benefits?

questions.follow_up_prompt: How could you work around that?
questions.question: Are there financial barriers that could limit your project?

questions.follow_up_prompt: How are those ecosystems affected?

questions.follow_up_prompt: How could you reduce that risk?
questions.question: What unintended environmental consequences could happen?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Is that a tradeoff you can live with?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would strengthening that lens look like?

question_bank.description: For projects that hit an unexpected blocker or need to change direction

questions.follow_up_prompt: What does that tell you?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What direction might it be pointing toward?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would it take to protect that part of the goal?
questions.question: What part of your original goal still feels important?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Did that change how you see the project?
questions.question: What assumptions did this challenge help you uncover?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would that stronger version look like?
questions.question: How might this redirect your project in a stronger direction?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What can you learn from what they tried?
questions.question: Who else has faced a similar barrier, and what did they try next?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What makes you say that?
questions.question: If you zoomed out, would this feel like a detour or a dead end?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would the first step toward that look like?
questions.question: What would resilience look like for your team right now?

questions.follow_up_prompt: How does that feel to name?
questions.question: What parts of this situation are outside your control?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Which of those feels most doable right now?
questions.question: What parts are fully within your control?

questions.follow_up_prompt: When could you do that?
questions.question: What small action could you take this week?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would you want to ask them?
questions.question: Who can you communicate with to clarify expectations?

questions.follow_up_prompt: How could you use that?
questions.question: What resources do you already have that you may have overlooked?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would you keep no matter what?
questions.question: If you reduced your scope slightly, what would still be meaningful?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would make that decision feel more confident?
questions.question: What is one decision your team can confidently make today?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What would it take to make that happen?
questions.question: What would progress, even tiny progress, look like?

question_bank.description: Specifically for En-ROADS carbon calculations. Step by step, one number at a time. Frame as discovery not calculation.

questions.follow_up_prompt: What does that action look like in real life?
questions.question: What specific action are you modeling in En-ROADS?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Does that change make sense to you?
questions.question: What does En-ROADS show happens when that lever moves?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Does that unit make sense in this context?
questions.question: What unit is the model using, and what does that unit represent in the real world?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Where would we find that number?
questions.question: If we slow this down, what is the very first number we need?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Is that number reasonable? How can you check?
questions.question: Where did that number come from — a source, an estimate, or an assumption?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What does each piece represent?
questions.question: If the number feels big, can we break it into smaller pieces?

questions.follow_up_prompt: What direction is it moving, and is that the direction you expected?
questions.question: What does the change look like visually on the graph?

questions.follow_up_prompt: Does that story surprise you?
questions.question: If we explain this result in plain language, what story is the data telling?
